title: The ball came back but my dog was asleep 🐕
style_prompt: cinematic horror film still, dark moody blue-teal grade, one bright light source, well exposed, 35mm film grain, realistic, no text, no watermark, no faces
hook_text: At 11:20 p.m. I threw the ball into the dark hallway and it came back.

scenes.narration: At 11:20 p.m. I threw the ball into the dark hallway and it came back.
My dog loves that game. I throw. He runs. He drops the ball by my feet. Always the same wet thud.

shots.prompt: cozy living room at night with a sofa and a lamp, a dog bed, no person

scenes.narration: So when the ball rolled back out of the dark, I did not look up. I just reached for it.

shots.prompt: tennis ball on a wooden floor in lamplight, dark hallway behind, no person

scenes.narration: It was wet. And cold. Cold like it had been held by something that does not warm things.

shots.prompt: close view of a wet tennis ball on a wooden floor, cold light, no person

scenes.narration: Then I looked up. On the sofa, my dog was fast asleep. Curled up. Paws twitching. He had never moved.

shots.prompt: sleeping dog curled up on a sofa in a dim living room, no person

scenes.narration: Something had caught the ball. Something had thrown it back. Something that knew exactly how this game goes.

shots.prompt: dark hallway doorway with faint shapes in the shadows, no face

scenes.narration: I threw the ball again, very softly, because I did not know what else to do. Into the dark. It landed. A pause.

shots.prompt: tennis ball in the air in a dim living room towards a dark hallway, no person

scenes.narration: Then I heard the thud. Wet. Close. And footsteps on four legs, coming towards me, in the hallway, not in the sofa.

shots.prompt: dark hallway with the sound of something low moving, faint silhouette on the floor, no face

scenes.narration: My dog woke up. He looked at the hallway. And he started to growl at me.

shots.prompt: dog on a sofa looking toward the camera in a dim room, glowing eyes in lamp light, no person

scenes.narration: So tell me. Do you throw the ball once more, or grab your dog and leave?
